item.title: Public interest at heart of CPC self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
Public interest at heart of CPC self-governance Maintaining Party's fundamental bond with the people seen as key to leadership Before leaving a budget hotel in Fuping county, Hebei province, on Dec 29, 2012, Xi Jinping instructed his staff to make sure the dinner bill was paid, recalled Jia Chunhong, the hotel's catering manager. The meal itself was simple: four homestyle dishes, soup, some staple foods, and no alcohol served. The two-day field trip to Fuping county came just six weeks after Xi was elected general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee. Only 25 days before the dinner, Xi had chaired a meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee that adopted the eight-point decision on improving work conduct and maintaining close ties with the people, setting out requirements for officials on matters ranging from grassroots research to meetings and official receptions. At that meeting, Xi said, "Only when we are under pressure and supervision can people enjoy a more comfortable and satisfying life and have a higher opinion of us." The eight-point decision became an early step in the CPC's broader drive to exercise full and rigorous self-governance, extending strict requirements in areas ranging from officials' conduct to Party building as a whole. At a gathering marking the CPC's 95th anniversary in July 2016, Xi warned that the Party could eventually lose its qualifications to govern if it failed to enforce strict self-governance and address serious internal problems that drew strong public complaints. In the same speech, Xi described standing with the people as the Party's fundamental political position, saying that the people's support, approval, satisfaction and consent should serve as the fundamental criteria for evaluating its work. For Xi, the Party must always guard against and correct with resolve the practices the people oppose and resent. "We will focus on enhancing the Party's capacity for long-term governance, preserving its advanced nature and integrity, and maintaining its close bond with the people," he said while addressing a gathering marking the CPC's 105th anniversary in July this year. Xie Maosong, a senior researcher at Tsinghua University's National Institute of Strategic Studies, said that full and rigorous Party self-governance was not simply about enforcing discipline, but about preserving the CPC's fundamental bond with the people. "Public oversight and the Party's self-reform reinforce each other. Both are essential to ensuring that power is exercised in the public interest and that officials remain committed to serving the people," he said. Ultimately, the effectiveness of Party building should be measured by whether it strengthens public trust, protects the people's interests and keeps the Party closely connected with those it serves, Xie said. Former Ethiopian president Mulatu Teshome said the CPC's internal rules and discipline have made the Party "stronger and stronger", helping sustain its leadership and maintain policy continuity in China's development. He said that corruption could drive a wedge between a governing party and the people it served, eroding public trust and undermining national development. Teshome stressed that misconduct by officials should not be tolerated and that maintaining close ties with the people is essential to effective governance. Concrete benefits Gulnar Shaimergenova, director of the China Studies Center in Kazakhstan, said stricter Party governance should translate into better-performing institutions and concrete benefits for the public. "Full and rigorous Party self-governance goes beyond combating corruption. It is also about improving the way institutions function, ensuring that officials fulfill their responsibilities and that government policies produce tangible benefits for the people," she said. She pointed to the CPC's eight-point decision as an effort to tackle formalism and bureaucratic inefficiency, allowing officials to devote more time to employment, public services and other everyday concerns, rather than unnecessary paperwork and procedural formalities. Beyond improving work practices, Shaimergenova said the real test is whether officials can deliver lasting improvements in people's lives. "Effective administration should not be measured simply by economic indicators or the number of policies introduced, but by whether development produces sustainable improvements in people's well-being," she said. That emphasis also underpins this year's Party-wide education campaign on establishing and practicing a correct view of governance performance, which shows China's unequivocal philosophy — governance is for the people. "Ultimately, I believe the people-first principle becomes meaningful when it is reflected not only in strategic documents, but also in the everyday conduct of officials and in improvements that citizens can genuinely experience," she said. Tongan Deputy Prime Minister Viliami Uasike Latu said the CPC's internal governance mechanisms help hold individual members accountable for their conduct and ensure that they fulfill their responsibilities. Having visited China more than five times, Latu said he was impressed by the emphasis that Chinese leaders have placed on listening to public concerns and remaining accountable to the people. Nigerian lawmaker Satomi Alhaji Ahmad said that clean governance requires leaders to put their people's interests ahead of their own. "They put the country first," he said, praising what he saw as Chinese leaders' commitment to serving the public, rather than pursuing personal interests. He also stressed that ordinary people should benefit from good governance through better access to education, healthcare and other essential services. That concern for public interest is also reflected in efforts to tackle corruption and misconduct at the grassroots level. Since 2024, China's top disciplinary and supervisory authorities have led a nationwide campaign targeting misconduct and corruption that directly affect people's livelihoods. Figures reported in October showed that since the campaign began, authorities nationwide had investigated and dealt with 2.253 million instances of misconduct and corruption affecting the public and disciplined 1.555 million people. Disciplinary and supervisory bodies had also helped resolve 6.98 million pressing problems affecting the public, in areas including education, healthcare and other essential services. Noticeable change Former British lawmaker Mark Logan, who has followed China's development for about two decades, said he has witnessed a marked change in the country's approach to corruption. "You can definitely say today that China has much less corruption," he said. "There's a real focus on delivering for people," he added.

item.title: Robots wow travelers over weeklong holiday
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
Robots wow travelers over weeklong holiday Robots poured tea, played table tennis and answered children's questions about marine animals at a theme park in South China during this year's National Day holiday from Oct 1 to 7. Elsewhere, machines served coffee and ice cream, helped tourists scale mountains and prepared millions of meals. The holiday rush gave China's robotics manufacturers an opportunity to introduce their machines "face to face" with consumers, as tourist attractions, retailers and restaurants explored new ways to draw visitors and enhance services. At Chimelong Spaceship Park in Hengqin, Guangdong province, more than 300 robots developed by Shanghai-based AgiBot were deployed across over 100 interactive locations, welcoming visitors and providing guided tours, science education and entertainment. "I didn't expect robots to pour tea or play table tennis," said Li Linlin, who was visiting from Guangzhou, Guangdong, with her two sons. "We originally came to see the spaceship-themed attractions and marine animals, but the two boys were most fascinated by the robots that could chat and play with them." The deployment, which began in September, forms part of a 10-year strategic partnership between AgiBot and Chimelong Group. Rather than renting machines for holiday performances, the park purchased them for permanent use, allowing the partners to develop new attractions and refine the technology through daily interactions with visitors. "Technology is fast becoming a new tourism draw for China," said Wu Liyun, a professor at the China Academy of Culture and Tourism at Beijing International Studies University, adding that foreign visitors increasingly seek to experience how smart technologies are being integrated into everyday life. The growing interest is opening commercial opportunities for China's robotics industry, particularly in tourism, retail and other consumer services. An estimate based on publicly announced projects suggests that nearly 30 robotics firms had entered these sectors, with thousands of humanoid and other embodied robots in use during the weeklong holiday. Such applications are also a focus of China's broader push to use technology to expand spending on services. Guidelines released by the Ministry of Commerce and eight other departments on Oct 19 called for wider commercial applications of embodied artificial intelligence, as well as new cultural and tourism products and smart services using AI and other technologies. The Ministry of Culture and Tourism has selected 14 projects to pilot AI applications in the sector, aiming to develop approaches that can be adopted nationwide, Zhou Hanping, an official with the ministry's industrial development department, said at a news conference on the policy. For robot manufacturers, daily use at tourist attractions provides a practical test of both technical performance and consumer appeal. Wang Chuang, senior vice-president at AgiBot, told Xinhua Finance that simple games such as rock-paper-scissors and table tennis had attracted greater visitor interest than some technically demanding demonstrations. The company therefore plans to adjust the activities regularly based on visitor feedback and usage data. AgiBot also aims to make its robots less dependent on human supervision. Xiong Yan, co-president of AgiBot, said the park initially needed roughly one staff member for every three robots, although staffing requirements varied by specialized tasks performed. The company aims to reduce that requirement to one employee for every 10 robots, and eventually one for every 20, through improved automation and operational management. Reducing supervision and maintenance costs could make large-scale deployments more commercially feasible. Other manufacturers are expanding into retail. Chinese robotics maker Galbot has introduced more than 200 automated retail stations at locations including Beijing's Summer Palace, West Lake in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, and Gulangyu Island in Xiamen, Fujian province. Robots at the stations handle customer orders and product deliveries. Wearable exoskeleton robots are serving a different need — helping tourists walk longer distances with less physical effort at destinations including Taishan Mountain in Shandong province and Xi'an's ancient city wall in Shaanxi province. Beyond tourist attractions, specialized robots are already performing high-volume tasks hidden from customer view in restaurant kitchens, where efficiency and consistency matter more than entertainment. Chinese cooking robot manufacturer Xianglu Robotics said 12,741 of its automated cooking machines were working across 334 cities during the holiday, completing nearly 6 million stir-frying tasks. The company estimates that the output was enough to serve approximately 18 million diners, based on an average of three people per cooking cycle. In a written response to China Daily, Xianglu said the cooking figures were collected through its operating data platform, while batch sizes ranged from meals for individual restaurant customers to larger quantities used in institutional catering. It said cooking volumes had risen year-on-year, largely because more machines had been installed, although it did not provide comparable per-machine utilization figures. The wider commercial potential of robots in tourism is still being tested. Liang Zengxian, a tourism professor at Sun Yat-sen University, told Southern Finance that robots could complement rather than replace human performers, providing new forms of interaction and entertainment. Liang said integrating robotics with tourism could bring measurable economic benefits, although more real-world applications would be needed to fully demonstrate their commercial value.

item.title: Shanghai indices begin updated rules
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
Shanghai indices begin updated rules Expert: 15% cap can keep a behemoth from 'kidnapping' overall market The latest compilation adjustments to the major indices on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, which took effect on Monday, will help further cushion market volatility and lower risks, which is of great importance at a time of global downward pressure, said experts. Two major changes have been implemented, according to the latest revision details announced in late September. First, a constituent's weight is now capped at 15 percent. Second, the timing for removing risk-warning counters from the indices has been moved earlier. Previously, a stock was taken from the index on the first trading day after the second Friday of the month following the date the risk warning took effect. Now it is dropped on the first trading day after the second Friday of the month following the date the risk warning was issued. Tian Lihui, a finance professor at Nankai University, compares the two practices to a "flow-control valve" and "filter" for the indices. The 15-percent cap can prevent one behemoth company from "kidnapping" the overall market performance due to its huge size. Bringing the removal date forward ushers disqualified counters out of the sample pool more efficiently. "Amid higher downward pressure, the market is more sensitive to any factors that might aggravate fluctuations. The latest adjustments can cleanse the index ecosystem at the algorithmic level, ensuring the indices objectively and fairly reflect overall quality even in a weak market," Tian said. Four major indices — including the SSE Composite Index and the STAR Composite Index — are subject to the 15-percent cap limit. Guo Shiliang, an independent financial commentator, said the new rule is mainly an adjustment to the compilation rules of the SSE series of indices rather than a cap applied uniformly on all A-share market indices. Given that the SSE Composite Index's weight composition is relatively balanced and the weight of any single heavyweight stock is far below the 15-percent cap, the impact on the SSE Composite Index's constituent shares is fairly limited, and the room for subsequent constituent weight adjustments will be relatively small. By contrast, the impact on weight adjustments for the tech-focused STAR Composite Index's constituent stocks will be larger. "Take memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies as an example. Prior to the new rule, the company's market-cap weight would have exceeded 20 percent once formally added to the STAR Composite Index, well above the 15-percent cap. The new rule will effectively reduce the index's overreliance on any single stock," Guo said. As for the adjustment to risk-warning stocks, Yang Delong, chief economist at First Seafront Fund, said that the liquidity of these companies may deteriorate in a weak market. Bringing the removal date forward helps shorten the time that passive products are stuck holding problem stocks and reduces the impact costs of concentrated rebalancing, thereby protecting the interests of investors holding funds that track the index, Yang said. This move represents another major adjustment in SSE indices since July 2020, when special treatment stocks — those with abnormal financial or operational situations — were removed from the sample pool and the inclusion of new stocks was delayed. Analysts from Guosen Securities said that the indices' long-term representation and investability are likely to steadily improve after the latest changes. Wu Xinkun, chief strategist at Guosen Securities, admitted there is short-term downward pressure on the A-share market, which is a combined result of external and internal factors. Rising oil prices amid geopolitical tensions in the Middle East — as well as the high inflation and interest rates in the United States — have suppressed the pricing of risky assets globally. In the domestic market, investor sentiment for the tech sector has not bottomed out while the market is still awaiting more capital inflows. The market fluctuation is thus magnified, Wu said. But the outlook on the A-share market's mid- to long-term performance is by no means pessimistic. Companies' profitability is improving, and more long-term capital will be ushered into A shares, providing support for a rebound likely to take place this quarter, he added. shijing@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Long March's grit, resolve lauded
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
Long March's grit, resolve lauded Red Army's achievements could inspire people around the world, diplomats say The leadership of the Communist Party of China, support of the people and unwavering resolve enabled the Red Army to overcome overwhelming odds on the Long March, laying the foundations for modern China, foreign diplomats said on Monday, as they called for the same determination to address today's global challenges. Diplomats and envoys from 106 embassies and five international organizations in China toured The Great Expedition, an exhibition at the Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution in Beijing that commemorates the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March. The Long March was a strategic military maneuver carried out by the Workers' and Peasants' Red Army of the CPC from 1934 to 1936. The troops crossed rivers, mountains and grasslands to break the siege by the Chinese Kuomintang forces. Somphone Sichaleune, the Lao ambassador to China, identified the CPC leadership, the solidarity of the Chinese people and their support for the Red Army as crucial to the victory. He said history provided a "vivid example for the new generation", adding that understanding it matters as people embark on new journeys to build their country, while its significance extended to people elsewhere pursuing national liberation and progress. Stephen Jackson, the United Nations' resident coordinator in China, highlighted a "sense of determination and the ability to take the long view", linking these qualities to China's long history of overcoming challenges. He described the two-year Long March as an extraordinary feat of determination and endurance. "We need that kind of determination in the world. And China is showing it," he said, calling for renewed commitment to multilateralism, international cooperation and a shared future for humanity. Hussam Al Husseini, the Jordanian ambassador to China, said that witnessing China's current development has deepened his appreciation for the sacrifices made during the Long March and the resilience and determination of the Chinese people that helped lay the foundations of modern China. "Many of the sacrifices we don't understand until later," he said. He described the march as "an amazing story of determination" and resolve, noting that despite the severe hardships they faced, the Chinese people maintained clear goals. Hodan Osman Abdi, the Somali ambassador to China, said that she had learned about the Long March mainly from books. Tracing the route of the march at the exhibition and learning about its pivotal moments gave her a deeper understanding of the distance traveled and the hardships overcome. "I believe it really showed the Chinese people and different generations what they can achieve with perseverance and hard work, despite the odds," she said. The achievements of the Red Army amid scarce resources could inspire people worldwide, Abdi added. Luamanuvae Albert Mariner, the Samoan ambassador to China, said the exhibition highlighted "the values of perseverance, determination and courage" that continue to influence China's leadership. In his welcoming address to the diplomats, Hong Lei, China's assistant foreign minister, said the Long March spirit was a shared asset of world civilizations, with its values reflecting aspirations for truth, justice and peace. China is ready to work with other countries for peace and development, he added. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or award

Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or award Share - WeChat
LONDON -- Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or award on Monday, becoming England's first winner in 25 years. Alexia Putellas won the women's Ballon d'Or after leading FC Barcelona to four trophies last season, before joining London City Lionesses in the summer. This is her third women's Ballon d'Or award after 2021 and 2022.

item.title: Quake-hit county steps up resettlement
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured after the earthquake. Sixteen people were killed and 76 others injured after the earthquake. Electricity and communications have been restored in some villages in the hardest-hit areas of Drachen county. China's natural resources departments are carrying out an emergency screening for secondary geological hazards in the Xizang autonomous region following a deadly earthquake on Thursday. They have now completed surveys of all hazard sites within 50 kilometers of the epicenter. The Ministry of Natural Resources activated a Level III emergency response on Friday morning quickly after a magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck Drachen county in Nagchu city in Xizang at 10:33 pm on Thursday. The earthquake, with a focal depth of 10 km, resulted in 16 deaths and 76 injuries. Emergency personnel included a seven-member team of experts from the ministry who will conduct field inspections alongside local professionals. A back-end team used pre- and post-quake satellite imagery to analyze 80 glacial lakes and 145 glaciers within the 50-km zone. The analysis showed no significant impact on glaciers or lakes, and no signs of glacial-lake outburst floods triggered by the earthquake. The ministry also launched an emergency surveying and mapping response to ensure the production of specialized imagery maps for severely affected areas. This included creating pre- and post-quake image comparisons for Maru and Gangche townships, providing three-dimensional mapping services for parts of Maru township, and conducting InSAR deformation analysis using radar imagery. The Xizang natural resources department also activated a Level II geohazard response, mapping hazard sites within 100 km of the epicenter. Drones, satellite navigation devices and other equipment were deployed for rapid aerial surveys. As of now, the natural resources system has deployed 78 people, 21 vehicles and 13 drones across 18 teams within the quake zone to assess the geological safety of temporary settlements, the slope stability around residential areas, and the deformation of known hazard sites. Surveys have also been conducted at 16 temporary housing sites, 77 residential clusters, and 19 existing protection works, identifying 157 geohazard sites, with 122 being preexisting and 35 newly detected, and implementing preventive measures in all high-risk locations. No casualties from secondary geological hazards have been reported. Building on the completion of surveys within 50 km of the epicenter, the teams are now expanding their investigation with simultaneous assessments underway. After a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Drachen county in Nagchu, southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, on Thursday, Du Guoping, owner of a dumpling restaurant in Shigatse, postponed the opening of his two new restaurants and headed to the disaster zone with his staff. "It took only about 10 minutes to make the decision that we would go to Drachen and cook dumplings for earthquake-affected residents," Du said. The team loaded more than 1,500 kilograms of dumplings onto vehicles and set off from Shigatse at midnight on the night of the earthquake. Upon arrival, Du and his staff set up cooking equipment and prepared dumplings for rescue workers and affected residents. "Make sure everyone gets enough dumplings, and give children a couple more," Du kept telling his staff. Du and his staff did not eat any of the dumplings themselves. After a full day of cooking, they had some instant noodles — their only meal of the day. At night, the six team members of Du squeezed into two vehicles to rest. "We will cook all the dumplings we brought," Du said. "We feel honored to be able to contribute in our own way." Resettlement and medical care efforts are progressing in an orderly manner in Drachen county of Nagchu city in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, which was hit by a magnitude 7 earthquake on Thursday, as authorities stepped up efforts to provide temporary housing and restore normal life in the affected areas. As of Saturday, major roads in the county remained open to traffic, and power supply to earthquake-affected areas had been fully restored after repairs, reports said. The earthquake affected 13,673 residents of 34 administrative villages in Maru and Gangchen townships, where the average altitude is 4,800 meters. A total of 12,489 people have been relocated, including 7,600 from Maru and 4,889 from Gangchen, accounting for about 91.3 percent of the affected population. By Saturday, all 12,489 people had been accommodated in 1,830 tents at 35 resettlement sites across the county. Given the high altitude and low temperatures, local authorities are setting up prefabricated houses equipped with heating stoves to improve living conditions for affected residents. Relief supplies allocated by central, regional, municipal and county authorities have been delivered to the affected areas, totaling 60,518 items or sets across 20 categories. The supplies include 4,758 tents and 2,000 prefabricated housing units. As of 5 pm on Saturday, the earthquake had left 16 people dead and 76 injured. All the injured had been taken to hospital for medical treatment. Of them, 40 were treated and discharged, while the others remained hospitalized, local officials said. Sonam Kyi, 40, who lived with 11 family members in a village in Maru township, said local government workers had arranged for them to stay in a tent at a resettlement site. "We are living in a tent with 10 beds and two stoves provided by the government, and it's warm inside," Sonam Kyi said. Nangshig Kyab and his family from Gangchen township were also safely relocated to a resettlement site. Nangshig Kyab said numerous cracks had appeared on the walls of his home, making it unsafe to live in, while the yak shelter and courtyard walls had collapsed. Township officials arrived at his village to carry out rescue operations within three hours of the earthquake and promptly evacuated residents, Nangshig Kyab said. By noon on Friday, government-delivered relief supplies had arrived in the village. "We were provided with tents, quilts, bedding, mattresses, heating stoves, instant noodles and other daily necessities, giving us a safe and warm temporary shelter," Nangshig Kyab said. By Sunday, the response had shifted toward resettlement and medical care, with construction of prefabricated houses underway. Tian Lihua, secretary of the Party branch for the Lhasa-Nyingchi area of the fourth branch of China Railway 21st Bureau Group Co, said more materials for prefabricated housing units were expected to arrive in batches on Sunday night and Monday. Once installed, the prefabricated houses provide better protection against wind and cold and offer better insulation than canvas tents, helping residents withstand the harsh conditions of the high-altitude plateau, Tian said. Meanwhile, a magnitude 5.7 aftershock struck Drachen county in Nagchu at 7:25 pm on Sunday, according to the China Earthquake Networks Center. BEIJING -- A 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen county of Nagchu city in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region at 7:25 pm Sunday (Beijing Time), according to the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC). The epicenter was monitored at 32.43 degrees north latitude and 93.99 degrees east longitude. The quake struck at a depth of 10 km. Emergency supplies and temporary housing are reaching residents in Gangchen township, one of the hardest-hit areas following Thursday night's magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county, Nagchu, Xizang autonomous region. China Railway 21st Bureau Group has delivered warm clothing, instant noodles, bottled water and tents to affected residents. Fourteen prefabricated housing units have arrived, with installation set to begin, while another 20 are expected Sunday night, Tian Lihua, Party branch secretary of the company's Lalin regional division, said. "Once installed, the prefabricated houses will provide better wind protection and insulation than tents, helping residents withstand the high-altitude cold," Tian said. Gangchen Township sits at an elevation of more than 4,600 meters, where nighttime temperatures can drop to minus 6 C. Nang Shigkyab, a local villager, said the family had been evacuated to safety. Relief supplies, including tents, bedding, mattresses and heating stoves, arrived the following day. "We now have safe, warm temporary accommodation. Our lives are stable, and we feel reassured," Nang said. Tashi Samdrub, 37, said a rescue team had provided him with 15 sacks of yak dung fuel free of charge, enough to keep his family's tent warm for about a month. Repair crews from China Mobile Tietong's Xizang branch have restored home broadband and dedicated line services in the county seat of Drachen, as well as a key mobile base station in Maru Township near the epicenter, following the magnitude-7.0 earthquake on Thursday night. The branch dispatched eight emergency vehicles and 17 repair workers to the affected area, which has an average elevation of about 4,800 meters. After 12 hours of work, crews also established a dedicated communication line for the emergency command center, deployed emergency fiber-optic cables and expanded network capacity to support rescue operations. They also installed fiber-optic lines for more than 40 households in temporary housing areas, with efforts shifting toward maintaining stable communications during the recovery. Lhawang Chozang, a China Mobile employee at a service station in Maru Township, said six service stations had been set up across Drachen and Sog counties. "We have restored our network signals, but basic customer services are just as important," he said. The stations provide on-site assistance, free SIM-card replacements for residents who lost their cards in the earthquake, and measures to prevent service suspensions for affected residents and rescue workers, Lhawang said. The company said it would continue network inspections, signal optimization and communications support at temporary settlements during resettlement and post-disaster reconstruction. LHASA -- Rescue and relief efforts continue after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Drachen county of the city of Nagchu in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region, local authorities said Saturday. The earthquake, which struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday, has left 16 people dead and 76 others injured. The quake has also damaged or destroyed 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds. As of 11 am Saturday, all 76 injured people were receiving timely medical treatment, with five of the 11 people initially classified as seriously injured having improved to a mild condition, according to the local emergency command headquarters. Meanwhile, relief supplies and rescue personnel continue to arrive in the affected areas. As of 11 am Saturday, 52,450 items or sets of disaster relief supplies had been sent to the quake zone, while more than 2,500 rescue personnel were engaged in relief operations. The supplies include 4,651 tents, 2,000 prefabricated houses, 11,772 folding beds, 5,715 quilts and other cold-weather necessities. A large Wing Loong unmanned aerial vehicle has also arrived at the site. Authorities have established 35 temporary resettlement sites in the disaster zone. More than 1,600 personnel from Drachen county, 347 firefighters from the Nagchu fire and rescue detachment, and 530 police officers from the Nagchu public security bureau have been deployed, alongside vehicles and search-and-rescue dogs. Medical treatment and public health and epidemic prevention efforts are proceeding in an orderly manner, the headquarters said. As of 2 pm Saturday, the headquarters said 949 aftershocks had been recorded in the affected areas, including eight measuring 4.0 to 4.9 in magnitude and 33 measuring 3.0 to 3.9. All temporary speed restrictions on the quake-hit section of the Qinghai-Xizang Railway were lifted on Friday night, according to China Railway Qinghai-Xizang Group Co Ltd. A comprehensive inspection found no abnormalities, and trains resumed normal operations, the company said. Power supply in the quake-hit area was fully restored on Saturday night, according to the State Grid. State Grid Xizang Electric Power Co Ltd urgently dispatched teams to the affected area for emergency power restoration after the quake, the state-owned utility said. More than 300 personnel along with vehicles, power generation facilities and emergency equipment have been deployed as of Saturday to ensure power supply for the on-site command center, provide lighting for resettlement sites and restore damaged power lines. Local authorities said construction on the first batch of prefabricated houses in the quake-affected areas started at around 2 am Saturday. As more units arrive, residents currently staying in tents will gradually move into the better-insulated temporary housing. "We will ensure that affected residents have safe shelter, warm clothing and bedding, hot meals and clean drinking water," said Pan Zhiqing, Party chief of the Nagchu Municipal Emergency Management Bureau. At a hospital in Drachen's neighboring Sog county, many injured residents were sent there for treatment overnight. The hospital has arranged medical treatment and prepared hot meals and daily necessities for patients. Early Friday morning, Norbu Wangchen, a local resident in Sog county, brought more than 100 portions of Tibetan noodles, along with Tibetan tea and tsampa, to the hospital to help those affected by the earthquake. Help also came from the city of Shigatse, some 700 kilometers away from Drachen. Du Guoping, who was preparing to open two new restaurants in Shigatse, postponed the openings after learning of the earthquake and headed to the disaster zone with more than 1,500 kg of dumplings. His team set off at midnight on the night of the earthquake. After a bumpy journey, the team purchased additional supplies, including food containers and bottled water, along the way. After arriving, Du and his staff set up cooking equipment and prepared dumplings for rescue workers and affected residents. They worked during the day, and at night, the six team members squeezed into two vehicles to rest, keeping the heating on to ward off the high-altitude chill. With more than 500 kg of dumplings still remaining, Du said the team planned to stay for at least three days to cook all the food they brought. Watching firefighters, medical personnel and rescue teams race against time at the disaster site left a deep impression on him. "We feel honored to be able to contribute in our own way," he said. Following the magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county, Nagchu, Xizang autonomous region, on Oct 22, many temporary housing units have been rushed in from Lhasa, with workers racing to complete their installation. A local Tibetan sweet-tea cafe is serving free hot meals to affected people. Rescue and relief operations continued on Saturday in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, as emergency workers and volunteers rushed to help residents affected by Thursday night's magnitude-7.0 earthquake. The quake, which struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday, has killed 16 people and injured 76 others, with 339 houses reported collapsed, according to a regional government. Authorities said on Friday that three rounds of searches had been completed, with no people reported missing. The regional government upgraded its emergency disaster relief response to Level II, effective Friday, to strengthen rescue operations and assistance to affected residents. In some of the hardest-hit villages in Maru township, rescue teams have been searching damaged buildings, setting up temporary shelters and delivering essential supplies. Volunteers have also joined the relief effort, offering food and other assistance to displaced residents. Sonam Ngodrub, who runs a Tibetan restaurant in Nagchu, traveled to one of the affected villages after the earthquake. "I run a Tibetan restaurant, and there isn't much else I can do apart from helping others," he said. "Every day, I can provide 100 to 150 kilograms of Tibetan noodles free of charge, along with roasted barley flour and sweet tea." Police officers and auxiliary personnel dug through rubble with their bare hands to rescue trapped residents in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, after a magnitude-7.0 earthquake struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday. A 45-member team from the county public security bureau set out at about 11 pm and traveled 85 kilometers, reaching the severely hit villages in Maru township at 12:30 am on Friday. "The only thing on our minds was getting the trapped residents out as quickly as possible," said Tsering Dawa, an officer with the county public security bureau. With temperatures dropping to minus 6 C and aftershocks continuing, 10 officers cleared fallen rocks from roads while the remaining 35 personnel searched for survivors in groups of three. They used drones to assess the damage, coordinated with village officials to check residents' whereabouts, and searched homes one by one. Before heavy machinery arrived, the rescuers used wooden poles to support unstable structures and squeezed through twisted door and window frames to reach trapped residents. They searched more than 200 households and helped transport injured people to hospital. After daybreak, the team directed traffic, transported supplies and set up more than 30 tents to shelter residents. DRACHEN, Xizang - Sixteen people have been killed and 76 others are injured following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Drachen county of the city of Nagchu in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region at 10:33 pm on Thursday, local authorities said. The quake has also damaged or destroyed 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, according to a press conference held on Friday afternoon by the information office of the Nagchu municipal government. Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured, urging every effort to minimize casualties. Xi also called for close monitoring of seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters, as well as proper accommodation for affected residents and swift repairs to damaged infrastructure. Premier Li Qiang called for solid disaster prevention and response efforts, while the Ministry of Emergency Management (MEM) and authorities in Xizang have mobilized resources for rescue and relief operations. China has allocated 50 million yuan (about $7.5 million) in emergency disaster relief funds and earmarked another 30 million yuan for recovery efforts. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III. More than 5,000 personnel have been deployed to the front lines of the disaster relief operation, working in teams responsible for search and rescue, medical treatment, temporary shelter and the provision of essential supplies. An emergency command headquarters has been established on the front lines to coordinate relief efforts. As of 10 am Friday, 12,489 residents have been evacuated. After three rounds of comprehensive door-to-door checks, no missing persons had been reported as of 6 pm Friday, according to the emergency command headquarters. In a village of Maru township, one of the hardest-hit areas near the epicenter, Xinhua reporters saw many houses completely collapsed, while others sustained extensive wall damage. Rows of emergency tents were erected in an open, safe area below the village. Half of villager Trinley's house collapsed, burying many of his belongings beneath the rubble. Two white tents were set up in his courtyard. "After the earthquake, our biggest concerns were where to stay and what to eat," Trinley said. "The government provided us with supplies including emergency tents, water and instant noodles," he added. The MEM said that on top of the 5,000 relief items previously allocated by the central government, an additional 5,000 central relief items, including tents, coats and folding beds were allocated. By coordinating efforts with other relief agencies and companies, the ministry said that it has also promptly allocated 43,000 other relief items, including mobile toilets, heating stoves, food and fuel, to ensure that affected people are properly resettled. The Red Cross Society of China has dispatched a working team to the disaster-hit area to guide local relief efforts. It has also allocated 3,800 sets of supplies, including family relief kits, hygiene kits, heaters, tents, jackets, folding beds and quilts. The society has additionally allocated 50 emergency toilet units to support affected residents and coordinated with the Chinese Red Cross Foundation to provide 500 family relief kits, 500 hygiene kits and more than 1,000 cartons of food to the quake-hit area. The China Charity Federation, one of the country's most influential charity organizations, has urgently allocated 3 million yuan to support emergency rescue endeavors. RESCUE CHALLENGES The earthquake zone has an average elevation of nearly 4,800 meters. The high-altitude, cold and low-oxygen environment, secondary disaster hazards and aftershock risks pose challenges to the relief efforts, local authorities said at the press conference. Deng Xiaogang, a rescuer with Nagchu's fire and rescue team, said that beyond the low temperatures and low oxygen levels, the biggest challenge was that the epicenter was in a pastoral area, where residents live far apart, making search-and-rescue operations more time-consuming in the initial stages. Some herding sites are up in the mountains, and the terrain is rugged, said Jigme Dorje, deputy head of the Drachen county public security bureau. "At first, machines could not reach these places, so we had to climb up and dig through the rubble with our hands, wearing only gloves," he said. Local authorities said that rescue teams will continue to take precautions to overcome difficulties in relief operations. Nighttime temperatures in the quake zone are low. Earthquake-triggered hazards such as landslides, collapses and falling rocks are currently the main secondary disaster risks. Earthquake monitoring, meteorological and emergency management departments, meanwhile, are coordinating closely to issue timely warnings of aftershocks and adverse weather conditions. Local authorities have launched round-the-clock intensified monitoring of key sites, including mountainsides, reservoirs, power stations, rivers, structurally unsafe buildings and telecommunications base stations. Emergency repairs are also underway, with damaged telecommunications and power facilities gradually being restored. Pan Zhiqing, Party secretary of Nagchu's emergency management bureau, said that in follow-up rescue work, personnel will be assigned to accompany rescue teams to inspect geological hazards along mountains and roads. Dangerous areas will be immediately cordoned off, and people and vehicles will be prohibited from passing. Transportation authorities will monitor road damage in real time, promptly repair and reopen blocked sections, and ensure smooth traffic flow. They will continue to coordinate with meteorological and natural resources departments and issue risk warnings, Pan added. China Telecom, China Mobile and China Unicom mobilized emergency repair teams, vehicles and equipment overnight, dispatching personnel to the quake-hit areas to restore communications services and inspect network facilities. All telecommunications base stations disrupted by the earthquake in Drachen county had been restored as of 10:30 am Friday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. The 7.0-magnitude earthquake was an extensional rupture, according to experts with the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC). "An extensional fracture, in simple terms, occurs when the crust is stretched horizontally and, under tension and gravity, faultage slides downward along existing faultage, forming fractures and rupture surfaces," said Han Yanyan, a senior engineer with the earthquake prediction department of the CENC. President Xi Jinping has urged all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured, in order to minimize casualties after a magnitude 7 earthquake rocked Drachen county in Nagchu, Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. The quake, which struck at 10:33 pm on Thursday at a depth of 10 kilometers, killed 16 people, injured at least 76, and damaged or flattened 339 houses, with search for survivors continuing on Friday. In an instruction issued on Friday morning, Xi noted that the affected county is at a high altitude with low temperatures, emphasizing the need to closely monitor seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters. It is imperative to dispatch emergency rescue supplies, properly accommodate the affected residents, and repair damaged infrastructure as quickly as possible to safeguard people's lives and property, Xi said. In a separate instruction, Premier Li Qiang called for swift assessment of the situation. Given the county's high altitude and the frequent aftershocks, Li urged the Ministry of Emergency Management and the China Earthquake Administration, together with relevant authorities, to strengthen seismic monitoring and forecasting, and step up disaster prevention and response efforts. Surveillance footage shared by local media showed buildings shaking violently as the temblor struck, with goods falling off shelves and residents rushing outdoors. In Maru township, one of the hardest-hit areas in Drachen, the ground cracked open and sections of a road sank, China Central Television reported. China's national comprehensive fire and rescue force has dispatched 350 personnel and 83 vehicles to support operations in the quake-hit areas. The national earthquake emergency response was upgraded on Friday to Level III — the third highest in China's four-tier system — while a separate Level III national natural disaster relief response was also activated. The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corp has deployed satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles to aid rescue efforts. The corporation said it is coordinating resources at its disposal to facilitate emergency communication and support imaging of the quake-hit areas. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management have jointly allocated 50 million yuan ($7.5 million) to support rescue and relief operations, while the National Development and Reform Commission has earmarked an additional 30 million yuan from the central budget to help restore damaged infrastructure and public service facilities. The Red Cross Society of China has allocated 3,800 units of relief supplies, including hygiene kits, heating stoves and cotton tents, along with 50 sets of emergency toilets. On the ground, rescue teams have been working relentlessly. In Gangchen township, one of the areas closest to the epicenter, rescuers launched a door-to-door search in the early hours of Friday. In Maru, a resident trapped in a damaged house was rescued around 2:20 am by firefighters who arrived from Drachen. On Friday afternoon, Nagchu Mayor Dondrub said at an on-site news briefing that emergency relief supplies from central and local authorities were being promptly delivered to the affected county. He said that 18 temporary resettlement sites have been set up, providing displaced residents with warm shelter, food, clothing, clean drinking water and medical care. A total of 12,489 people have been relocated, he added. Power supply and communication networks are being restored gradually in the hardest-hit areas. All 628 mobile base stations, which were knocked offline by the earthquake, were restored by 10:30 am on Friday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. Meng Linghe, Party chief of Drachen, said the quake-hit areas have an average elevation of nearly 4,800 meters, which means temperatures plummet after dusk. In addition to the freezing weather, the possibility of secondary disasters, such as landslides, poses grave risks, he said. As scattered snow showers are expected in the coming days, with ice and snow likely to cover high-altitude road sections, Meng urged rescue teams to remain alert and exercise caution when transporting personnel and supplies to the affected areas. Meanwhile, a magnitude 4.5 earthquake hit Zadoi county in neighboring Qinghai province at 10:14 pm on Friday, according to the China Earthquake Networks Center. The quake occurred at a depth of 10 km, with its epicenter located around 20 km from the epicenter of the Drachen temblor. Li Hongyang and Liu Boqian contributed to this story. BEIJING -- China has deployed satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to aid rescue efforts following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Thursday evening. The China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) said on Friday that immediately after the disaster, it coordinated and deployed satellite resources to conduct emergency communication support and imaging of the quake-hit area. The CASC said it has activated multiple high-throughput satellite internet emergency service lines for the Ministry of Emergency Management, local emergency management authorities, and major telecom operators. Additional service line terminals are on their way to the quake-hit area. In response to satellite imaging requests for quake relief, the CASC immediately mobilized Gaofen-4 and other satellites to observe the quake-hit area. As of 7 am (Beijing Time) Friday, it had delivered four pre-disaster images and three post-disaster images, providing strong support for rescue and relief operations and disaster assessment. According to the Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC), a UAV Wing Loong took off from an airport in Xigaze of Xizang autonomous region in the early hours of Friday and flew to the quake-hit area to carry out disaster observation and communication support missions. The AVIC said other Wing Loong teams are ready for deployment. Chinese People's Liberation Army Air Force also sent a UAV around midnight to the quake-hit area for disaster survey. Sixteen people were killed and 76 others injured after the earthquake struck Baqen county of Nagqu city in Xizang autonomous region at 10:33 pm Thursday, local authorities said on Friday. BEIJING -- The 7.0-magnitude earthquake that struck Baqen county of the city of Nagqu in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region on Thursday was an extensional rupture, according to experts with the China Earthquake Networks Center (CENC). The quake occurred at around 10:33 pm, causing heavy casualties. Focal mechanism solutions show the event was basically consistent with regional tectonic characteristics. The CENC explained that the collision between the Indian and Eurasian plates had caused the uplift of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, crustal shortening and thickening, and widespread plateau deformation. These processes are the main dynamic mechanism controlling tectonic deformation in the western part of the Chinese mainland. The interior of the plateau is subjected to both north-south compression and east-west extension, and two typical fault systems, trending roughly north-south and east-west, have developed there. "The epicenter is located within the Changtang block of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, about 2 km from the nearest fault, the Baqen-Riwoqe fault," Han said. Under such intense crustal deformation, the Changtang block and its surrounding fault zones are particularly active. Since 1900, the block has experienced six earthquakes of magnitude 7 or above, including this one. The largest was a 7.5-magnitude earthquake in Shuanghu on Nov 8, 1997. "Therefore, this earthquake was an energy release of the Changtang block," Han said. Authorities in Nagchu city, Xizang autonomous region, warned at a Friday news conference that aftershocks and secondary disasters remain major risks following a magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county on Thursday night. The quake had killed 16 people and injured 76, said Dondrub, mayor of Nagchu. The affected area averages nearly 4,800 meters in elevation, according to Meng Linghe, Drachen's Party secretary. Landslides, slope collapses, and falling rocks are the main secondary geological hazards. Low nighttime temperatures, scattered snow showers, and black ice on shaded high-altitude roads pose risks to rescue vehicles. Dondrub said inspections have covered 12 roads spanning more than 1,700 kilometers, 201 bridges, and 324 culverts. Officials identified 11 hazards and cleared rockfalls at seven road locations. Earthquake, meteorological, and emergency management departments are consulting and issuing aftershock and weather warnings, while police and transport authorities keep emergency routes open. Round-the-clock monitoring and emergency repairs cover mountain slopes, reservoirs, power stations, river channels, unsafe buildings, and telecommunications base stations. Authorities are inspecting mountain slopes and roads alongside rescue teams, Meng said. Dangerous areas will be cordoned off, and search operations will be kept away from steep slopes. Authorities will inspect geological hazard sites and vulnerable infrastructure hourly and continue issuing updated risk alerts, Dondrub said. China's transport authorities have stepped up road inspections and emergency support to ensure rescue vehicles can reach areas affected by a magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Southwest China's Xizang autonomous region. Roads in the quake-hit area are under traffic controls, with access maintained for rescue vehicles while other vehicles are temporarily barred, according to the Ministry of Transport. The earthquake struck Drachen county in Nagchu at 10:33 pm on Thursday. By 10 am Friday, 16 people had been killed and 76 injured, according to local authorities. The ministry activated a Level III emergency response for road transport at 9 am Friday and dispatched a team to coordinate rescue support and efforts to keep roads open. It is also coordinating with the Ministry of Finance to arrange emergency funding for road clearance and repairs. Level III is the second-lowest level in the ministry's four-tier response system, with Level I being the highest. Xizang's transport department activated its own Level II response after the earthquake. Local highway authorities deployed 178 personnel and 39 pieces of machinery to inspect affected sections of five national highways and seven provincial roads. They have checked 2,377 kilometers of roads, 295 bridges and 635 culverts. The inspections found varying degrees of damage along sections of national highway G345 and provincial highway S301. More detailed inspections of roads, bridges and other transport infrastructure are continuing. Emergency equipment is being sent to the disaster-hit area from reserve centers in Lhasa and Qamdo to help crews clear debris and repair roads. Crews from nearby construction projects run by centrally administered State-owned enterprises, along with other road maintenance teams, are on standby to provide additional support. Electricity and communications have been restored in some villages in the hardest-hit areas of Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, following a magnitude-7.0 earthquake on Thursday, according to the Xizang Communications Administration. State Grid Xizang Electric Power activated its emergency response and dispatched teams overnight to Gangche and Maru townships to inspect and secure power facilities. Electricity has been restored across the area surrounding the Maru township government offices. Phone and internet services have also returned to normal in two villages in the township. Being close to the earthquake's epicenter, they were among the most affected areas. According to the administration, the earthquake knocked 628 mobile base stations offline, accounting for 8.5 percent of the city's total. These stations have been restored as of 10:30 am Friday, bringing communications in the affected area back to pre-earthquake levels within 12 hours. The administration said 131 emergency repair personnel and 50 vehicles had been deployed to restore communications, along with 38 generators and other emergency equipment. Telecommunications networks in the disaster area are now operating normally, supporting the coordination of rescue operations. Earthquake authorities in Yunnan and Sichuan provinces have sent a dozen personnel to the affected area to assess the quake's intensity, verify damage, and conduct other emergency field operations. Sixteen people have been killed and 76 injured as of 1 pm Friday following Thursday's magnitude-7.0 earthquake in Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, officials said at a news conference Friday. Dondrub, mayor of Nagchu city, which administers the county, said rescuers had completed three rounds of searches, checking key areas and visiting residents in remote, scattered settlements. Authorities have set up 18 temporary shelters and relocated 12,489 people, he said. Due to the quake, 339 households have collapsed or been damaged, along with 20 livestock sheds. The immediate priorities are treating the injured and ensuring displaced residents have access to basic necessities, he said. Authorities will provide insulated tents and hot meals, with particular attention to older people, children, pregnant women, new mothers, and people with disabilities. Rescuers went door to door in villages near the epicenter of a magnitude-7.0 earthquake that struck Drachen county, Xizang autonomous region, looking for anyone in need of help. In Gangche township, one of the areas closest to the epicenter, rescue workers began searching for people trapped in their homes in the early hours of Friday morning. In Maru township, one of the hardest-hit areas, the earthquake cracked the ground and caused sections of road to sink, China Central Television reported. "Suddenly, there was a tremendous rumbling. For a moment, it felt as if hundreds of yaks were running at once," said Dzondru Tseltrim, a resident of Garuthang village in the county. His family had already gone to bed when the shaking began. Woken by the tremors, he heard cabinets and wooden pillars creaking inside the house. He rushed to wake his father, in his 80s, and helped him outside. Other family members soon followed. Fearing aftershocks, the family decided not to sleep indoors that night. They arranged for his father to rest in a car while the others prepared to spend the night in the courtyard. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management jointly allocated 50 million yuan to support rescue operations and assistance to affected residents, while the National Development and Reform Commission earmarked the additional 30 million yuan from the central budget to help restore damaged infrastructure and public service facilities. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III, while activating a separate Level IV national natural disaster relief response. China's national comprehensive fire and rescue force has dispatched a total of 350 rescuers and 83 vehicles for rescue operations. The emergency management ministry has guided Xizang's emergency management department in arranging for Wing Loong drone deployment to the quake-hit area for disaster reconnaissance. As of 6:30 am on Friday, 120 rescuers and 27 vehicles had arrived in the quake-hit area, while the remaining 230 rescuers and 56 vehicles from the Xizang fire and rescue corps were en route as reinforcements, having all entered Nagqu's administrative area. Earlier, as of 4:30 am on Friday, authorities had mobilized relief supplies at the central, regional, municipal and county levels, and delivered them in batches to the affected area. These supplies included 1,000 prefabricated housing units, 3,239 tents, 2,821 folding beds and 4,280 quilts, among other essentials.

item.title: Chinese opera hits big in small theaters
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
Tradition turns intimate as audiences get a close-up look at how various styles are created, performed, and expressed, Chen Nan reports. Li Chanchan and Fan Yuyan, two young students from the National Academy of Chinese Theatre Arts in Beijing, drew a crowd in a courtyard as they demonstrated a traditional jaw-dropping feat before one unleashed a burst of fire. The flames flared and vanished in an instant, prompting gasps and applause from spectators gathered among the courtyard's gray bricks and tiled roofs. The demonstration is a signature Qinqiang Opera stage skill: fire-breathing, known for its dramatic visual impact. Other performers demonstrated the sweeping spear movements of Peking Opera, offering a glimpse of the physical precision and theatrical spectacle that has sustained traditional Chinese opera for generations. At the 13th Xiqu Opera Black Box Festival, which opened at Star Theaters in Beijing on Oct 14, tradition is also being explored through more intimate, unexpected storytelling forms. The festival runs through Nov 22 and brings together 16 productions tailored for smaller theaters spanning 11 traditional Chinese opera genres, including Peking Opera, Kunqu Opera, Yuju Opera, Pingju Opera, and Cantonese Opera. The opening performance, The Face in the Mirror, a Huaiju Opera production, takes audiences into a world of illusion and psychological unease, asking what happens when people finally obtain what they desire.

item.title: World Bank director sees China's buzzwords
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-26
World Bank country director: What development keywords can a robot exhibition reveal about China? Over the past four plus decades and more, China has achieved rapid development and structural transformation, lifting 800 million people out of extreme poverty, and steadily raising incomes and welfare. Citing the World Robot Conference in Beijing as an example, Tatiana Rosito, World Bank country director for China, Mongolia, and Korea, noted that robotics is accelerating on the ground in China, boosting productivity and changing people's daily lives. She said she looks forward to China's 15th Five-Year Plan, including new productive forces, high-quality development, more and better jobs, and green transition. The World Bank's cooperation with China will focus on three pillars: promoting productivity and job growth, enhancing human capital for better jobs, and strengthening resilient infrastructure and natural capital. (Reporter: Li Wei; Video: Pan Yixuan, Cheng Zixin)
